title: Chana Masala
subtitle: North Indian spiced chickpea curry
excerpt: The great Punjabi chickpea curry: dried chickpeas soaked overnight, simmered in a deeply spiced tomato and onion masala until the sauce clings to the tender, slightly firm chickpeas. Tangy with amchur, warming with cumin and coriander.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chana masala (masala spiced chickpeas) is one of the definitive dishes of Punjabi cooking, eaten across North India and Pakistan as a street food, restaurant dish, and home staple. The dish uses kala chana (black chickpeas) in the most traditional versions but kabuli chana (the large white chickpeas common in Britain) is the more widely used variety internationally. The masala is built by caramelising onions until deep golden, then adding the tomatoes and spices and cooking them down until the oil separates from the paste — a technique known as bhunoing — which concentrates the flavour and removes the raw taste. Amchur (dried mango powder) provides a characteristic sourness; tamarind or lemon juice can substitute. Tinned chickpeas are a valid shortcut; dried chickpeas cooked from scratch have better texture.

content.text: Fry the onions very slowly and very well: pale gold onions make a pale, flat curry; deep chestnut-brown onions make a complex, dark one. Take them to the colour of beef stock cubes before adding the tomatoes. Cook the masala until the oil clearly separates from the tomato paste before adding the chickpeas; the separation shows that the spices have been properly cooked in.

items.preparation: 2 tins, drained; or 300 g dried, soaked overnight and boiled for 1 hour

content.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until they splutter. Add the onions and cook for 20 to 25 minutes over medium heat, stirring frequently, until deep golden brown. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the tomato purée, then the ground spices (cumin, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder). Cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until the oil separates visibly from the tomato paste and the mixture is thick and dark.

Add the chickpeas and 200 ml of water. Simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened and clings to the chickpeas. Add the garam masala and lemon juice. Taste and adjust the salt. Serve with fresh coriander, with roti or rice.
